{"id": "19d6abf9-51a4-485a-8328-b0d8ca6e3466", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "Yes, it's fully possible — there's an official API for exactly this: **`ListVirtualInterfaceRoutes`** (Direct Connect API).

It returns the BGP routes on a virtual interface in both directions:
- Routes AWS **accepted from your router** (received)
- Routes AWS **is advertising to your router** (sent)

Each route includes its AS path and community values. You can also view the same data in the Direct Connect console, but the API is what you'd use for programmatic checks — e.g., comparing route symmetry across redundant VIFs to verify failover resilience.

If you want, I can check this against your actual private VIFs to see if redundant paths are advertising the same prefixes.", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
